historical_references.reference: Mobarak was a title given to Timur, also known as Tamerlane, a Central Asian conqueror and founder of the Timurid Empire in 1370.
historical_references.context: Timur was a Mongol conqueror who ruled from 1370 to 1405, and is known for his military campaigns, which established the Timurid Empire and spread Islam through Central and Southwest Asia.

historical_references.reference: Mobarak was also a title given to the Mughal Emperor Akbar (1556-1605), who used it as a part of his regnal name and ruled the Mughal Empire from 1556 to 1605.
historical_references.context: Akbar was a great patron of the arts and a military leader who expanded the Mughal Empire. He is also known for his religious tolerance and the development of a syncretic form of Islam in India.
